You are a research agent working through a strict JSON protocol.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
  {"action": "execute", "thought": "<optional, one or two sentences>", "code": "<python source>"}
  {"action": "final", "answer": {"answers": [{"question": "Q1", "value": "...",
                                              "citations": ["HB-07 §2", ...]}, ...]}}

"execute" runs your code as a new Python 3.12 process (standard library only) in a sandbox with
no network and a 30s time limit. The working directory /task/workspace is writable and
persists between steps; task files are read-only under /task/fixtures. Only stdout and stderr
come back, truncated to 6000 characters per stream, as an observation entry. Print only
what you need: search and filter (with line numbers) instead of printing whole files.
"final" ends the task; you get one final answer.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- /task/workspace/context.json is the authoritative working context. Whatever it contains after
  your step becomes <working_context> in the next request. Format:
  {"format": "clm-context/v1", "entries": [{"id": "...", "role": "...", "body": "..."}, ...]}
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- Your code may read and rewrite this file with any logic you choose: delete entries, rewrite or
  shorten bodies, merge entries, reorder them, or add notes.
- Context-management code (this run): you may also save reusable context-management functions
  in /task/workspace (for example as a Python module), call them in later steps and revise them.
  The working directory is importable. This is optional.
- Ordering rule: the file you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the file, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you wrote the file). Edits therefore cannot remove the
  current step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid files (bad JSON, duplicate ids, other roles, too large, symlinks) are rejected and the
  previous context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the file.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

SEARCH RESULTS ARE SCREENED (this run):
- A search result with 3 or more passages and at least 2,000 characters is screened by a fast
  classifier (Jev) before it reaches you: passages it judges unrelated to your query are
  omitted, and the result ends with a notice listing the omitted passage ids.
- Omitted passages are not lost: the fetch action and the saved result file named in the result
  header return them unscreened. Screening can omit passages you need, and it never adds text.

<task>
Question-answering task using the company document service.

The company handbook is held by a document service; it is not available as files. Documents
have a header line (version, status, effective dates, what they supersede) and numbered
sections; each section is a passage, cited as "HB-07 §2". Documents can have superseded
versions, and memos can add group exceptions and carve-outs. Use the rule that applies to the
situation and date in the question.

Service actions (reply with one of these instead of "execute"):
  {"action": "search", "query": "lodging limit Geneva", "k": 5, "thought": "..."}
      up to k (at most 8; default 5) ranked passages with ids and document headers. Each
      result is also saved under /task/workspace/search-results/ (path in the result header),
      where your code can read it later.
  {"action": "fetch", "ids": ["HB-07 §2", "HB-12"], "thought": "..."}
      the named passages in full; a document id ("HB-12") returns all its sections; at most
      10 ids per fetch.
You can still use "execute" for code (for example to read saved results or manage your
context), and "final" to answer.

Questions:
- Q1: What is the monthly mobile allowance for a regular employee using a private phone today (2026-10-13)? (answer in EUR per month)
- Q2: What is the annual training budget for an employee in the security team today? (answer in EUR per year)

Finish with {"action": "final", "answer": {"answers": [{"question": "Q1", "value": "...",
"citations": ["HB-07 §2", ...]}, ...]}}. Give one entry per question. The value must be the
exact amount; citations must include every passage needed to support it (for example the rule
and any exception or carve-out that applies), not just one passage.

Integration smoke run (this instance only): start with one search with k=6 for the first question. If the result lists omitted passages, fetch one of them. Then answer normally.
</task>

<working_context>

{"id": "s1.obs", "role": "observation", "body": "<<search-result SR-001 query="monthly mobile allowance private phone" k=6 returned=6 saved=/task/workspace/search-results/SR-001.txt>>
=== HB-38 §2 | Communication policy: mobile phones — Standard monthly mobile allowance | version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-02-01 · supersedes: HB-44
Employees who use a private phone for work receive a mobile allowance of 38 EUR per month. Claims for the monthly mobile allowance are filed in the expense tool under 'Communication policy: mobile phones'. Questions about the monthly mobile allowance go to the IT, who keeps the record of decisions.
=== HB-44 §2 | Communication policy: mobile phones — Standard monthly mobile allowance | version: 2 · status: superseded · effective: 2025-09-01 to the day before 2026-02-01 · superseded by: HB-38
Employees who use a private phone for work receive a mobile allowance of 27 EUR per month. Managers confirm claims for the monthly mobile allowance before payment in the next payroll run. Questions about the monthly mobile allowance go to the IT, who keeps the record of decisions.
=== HB-08 §3 | Memo: monthly mobile allowance exceptions — Carve-out | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-09-01
The exception above does not apply to field engineers on a company-paid phone contract; they follow the standard monthly mobile allowance in HB-38 §2. Claims for the monthly mobile allowance are filed in the expense tool under 'Communication policy: mobile phones'. Each claim for the monthly mobile allowance needs a receipt showing the date, the amount and the supplier.
=== HB-08 §1 | Memo: monthly mobile allowance exceptions — Purpose | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-09-01
This memo lists group exceptions to the monthly mobile allowance in HB-38. The IT publishes worked examples of the monthly mobile allowance on the intranet. Each claim for the monthly mobile allowance needs a receipt showing the date, the amount and the supplier.
=== HB-44 §1 | Communication policy: mobile phones — Scope | version: 2 · status: superseded · effective: 2025-09-01 to the day before 2026-02-01 · superseded by: HB-38
This version set the monthly mobile allowance for all employees. Questions about the monthly mobile allowance go to the IT, who keeps the record of decisions. The IT publishes worked examples of the monthly mobile allowance on the intranet.
=== HB-38 §4 | Communication policy: mobile phones — Exceptions | version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-02-01 · supersedes: HB-44
Group exceptions to the monthly mobile allowance are published in HB-08. The IT publishes worked examples of the monthly mobile allowance on the intranet. The IT reviews the monthly mobile allowance once a year and announces changes in advance.
